provenance.original: TSA estimates the total cost burden for respondents by multiplying the number of application enrollees by the compensation rate for each respondent.  Multiplying the total time burden in hours, 12,859,023, by the loaded wage rate of $48.05, TSA estimates a total hourly cost burden estimate of $617,876,075 for respondents.  TSA multiplies the average time burden in hours, 4,286,341 by the hourly rate of $48.05 to estimate an average hourly cost burden of $205,958,692.  Table 17 below displays both 3-year total hourly cost burden and average hourly cost burden for TPAP respondents.

provenance.original: Freight Railroad Owner/operators: TSA estimates 28 freight railroad operators will conduct training for each employee once every 3 years, and their training records will be updated after each training.  TSA estimates an average of 45,385 current employees will be trained each year.  In addition, freight railroads will create 4,750 new training records per year due to employee turnover.  TSA estimates that each record has a time burden of 1 minute (0.01667 hours) to be created and/or updated.  TSA estimates the annual burden cost by multiplying the time burden by the industry compensation rate for an Administrative Assistant ($38.95).  The average annual cost of freight railroad carrier recordkeeping is depicted in Table 6.

provenance.original: TSA has estimated that 188 total respondent carriers will spend approximately 1 hour on quarterly reports, for a total of 752 hours per year.  Should the audit requirement be reinstated, TSA estimates that 113 carriers of the 188 total respondent carriers, collect fees from more than 50,000 passengers annually, and will be required to submit annual audits.  These carriers will spend approximately 20 hours on audit preparation, for a total of 2,260 hours annually.  The total annual hour burden for quarterly reports and annual audits is estimated at 3,012 hours.  TSA estimates the total annual responses to be 301 (188 plus 113, should the annual audit requirement be reinstated).

provenance.original: TSA estimates an average annual number of respondents completing the SOMQ and TSO Medical Clearance Form of approximately 18,000.  TSA estimates the average time to complete the SOMQ online tool is 30 minutes (0.50 hours).  Previously the SOMQ was a written form, which took respondents approximately 45 minutes to complete.  The SOMQ has been transitioned to an online form, which is estimated to require 30 minutes to complete (a 15-minute reduction in time burden).  This results in an annual SOMQ burden hour of 9,000 hours (18,000 respondents x 0.50 hours).

provenance.original: To estimate how many new Cybersecurity Coordinators and alternate coordinators will need to be appointed each year, TSA first estimates the number of existing coordinators and alternates.  TSA accomplishes this by multiplying the number of Owner/Operators for each mode by 2 which results in 898 coordinators for freight rail (449 × 2), 484 for passenger rail (242 × 2), and 144 for OTRB (72 × 2).  TSA uses the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) turnover rates to estimate that approximately 4 percent of the current population of Cybersecurity Coordinators and alternate Cybersecurity Coordinators will separate from their positions and require replacement each year.  In addition, TSA estimates that approximately 9 percent of Cybersecurity Coordinators and alternate coordinators will need to submit updated contact information each year.  This results in approximately 13percent of Owner/Operators having to submit new or updated Cybersecurity Coordinator designations in a given year (4% due to turnover + 9% due to updated contact information).  Applying this percentage to the population of covered Owner/Operators results in 117 new Cybersecurity Coordinators per year for freight rail operators (898 Owner/Operators × 13%), 63 for passenger rail (484 Owner/Operators × 13%), and 19 for OTRB (144 Owner/Operators × 13%).  Table 2 presents the annual hour cost burden associated with the designation of new Cybersecurity Coordinators and alternates due to employee turnover.
